event.title: US Continues Strikes on Iran Amid Traffic Standstill in Strait of Hormuz
event.canonical_title: US Continues Strikes on Iran Amid Traffic Standstill in Strait of Hormuz
event.summary: The US has completed its seventh consecutive night of strikes against Iran as the conflict escalates 140 days in. An industry analyst reports that traffic has come to a halt in the Strait of Hormuz, with no vessels willing to transit the area due to the ongoing military actions. Recent attacks have resulted in significant casualties, with reports indicating 50 killed and 500 wounded this month alone.

timeline.title: US Conducts Airstrikes on Iran Following Deaths of Two Soldiers in Jordan
timeline.summary: The United States has launched a series of airstrikes against Iranian military targets in response to an attack that killed two American service members at a base in Jordan. The strikes, which are part of an ongoing military campaign, reportedly targeted Iranian coast surveillance and air defense facilities, as well as missile and drone storage sites. Iran claims that the US strikes resulted in significant casualties, with reports of at least 50 people killed and hundreds wounded.
key_facts: Two US service members were killed and one is missing following an Iranian missile and drone attack in Jordan.
The US strikes on Iran are a retaliation for the attack on the US base, marking the eighth consecutive night of US military action against Iran.
Iranian media reported explosions in several coastal cities as a result of the US airstrikes.

timeline.title: Pentagon Confirms Deaths of Two US Soldiers in Jordan Following Iranian Attack
timeline.summary: The Pentagon has identified two active-duty US soldiers killed in an Iranian strike on a US base in Jordan. The attack occurred on Friday, resulting in the deaths of the soldiers and injuries to four others. This incident has prompted a series of retaliatory strikes by the US against Iranian targets, escalating tensions in the region.

timeline.title: Pentagon Confirms Identity of Third US Soldier Killed in Iranian Attack
timeline.summary: The Pentagon has identified Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton, a 30-year-old from Fayetteville, North Carolina, as the third US soldier killed in a recent Iranian attack. He was reportedly involved in the disposal of a drone in northern Iraq when the incident occurred. This marks the 17th service member to be named in connection with this ongoing conflict.

timeline.title: US Intensifies Airstrikes on Iran Following Deaths of Service Members
timeline.summary: The United States has escalated its military operations against Iran, launching a new series of airstrikes after the deaths of three American soldiers in recent Iranian attacks. President Trump has vowed that Iran will face consequences for the killings, and US forces have targeted various military sites within Iran. The conflict has also seen retaliatory strikes from Iran against US allies in the region, heightening tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has conducted attacks on US allies in the region.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is the 2026 armed conflict involving U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran and Iranian retaliatory attacks on U.S. and regional targets. It began with large-scale strikes on February 28, 2026, expanded into a regional security and maritime crisis, and has continued despite ceasefire and diplomatic efforts.

facts.label: Start and parties
facts.value: The current conflict began on February 28, 2026, when the United States and Israel carried out major strikes in Iran; Iran subsequently announced attacks on U.S. military assets in the region.

facts.label: U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says it commenced Operation Epic Fury at the President's direction at 1:15 a.m. on February 28, 2026, describing its stated aim as dismantling Iran's security apparatus and prioritizing locations it considers imminent threats.

facts.label: Regional scope
facts.value: The conflict has affected Iran and neighboring states across the Gulf and Middle East; the UN reported Iranian attacks or reported impacts involving Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

facts.label: Strait of Hormuz and shipping
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz has become a central theater because it is a strategically important Gulf shipping route. CENTCOM said it began blocking maritime traffic entering and leaving Iranian ports on April 13, while the UN has warned that maritime incidents and threats to navigation heighten escalation risks.

facts.label: Diplomacy and legal context
facts.value: The UN has urged de-escalation, respect for the UN Charter and international humanitarian law. It reported that Qatar-mediated talks sought to implement a June 17 memorandum of understanding, but renewed strikes and counterstrikes underscored the fragility of those arrangements.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline tracks selected July 2026 U.S.-Iran military and Strait of Hormuz developments; it does not attempt to catalog all strikes, casualties, diplomatic exchanges, or regional consequences of the wider war.
